claims.assertion: Swaruu (9) says stellar navigation uses frequency maps, where a location is its frequency rather than a physical coordinate.
claims.speaker: Swaruu (9)

claims.assertion: Swaruu describes perceived density as an observer’s processing capacity; observers cannot perceive frequencies beyond their range.
claims.speaker: Swaruu (9)

claims.assertion: She says a planet’s exact frequency harmonics provide starship navigation data, and frequency maps can represent locations or situations.
claims.speaker: Swaruu (9)

claims.assertion: She describes inserting objects or situations into other contexts by matching frequencies; the calculations require powerful nonbinary computers with particle nano-accelerators.
claims.speaker: Swaruu (9)
claims.qualifiers: Object harmonics need compatibility, while situations require more precise amalgamation.
